title: Triggers, Pagers, Cutouts, Commitment & Composed Color
description: Five live drops: a scroll-triggered (not scrubbed) CSS animation, a multicol book pager, ransom-note collage type, interruption-proof micro-interactions, and a self-deriving color palette.

drops.title: Scroll Triggers 2.0
drops.description: Chrome's new animation-trigger property fires a fixed-duration animation on scroll-threshold crossing — contrasted live against classic scroll-driven scrubbing.
drops.concept: Scroll-driven animations tie progress directly to scroll offset; the new animation-trigger CSS property instead behaves like a declarative Intersection Observer, playing a fixed-duration animation once per crossing with play-forwards/reset or play-once/none semantics. This drop demonstrates both trigger actions plus a direct side-by-side comparison against scrubbing.
drops.source: Chrome for Developers blog — 'CSS scroll-triggered animations are coming!'

interaction.mouse: Scroll through the page to fire each trigger pattern
interaction.click: Use the debug panel to replay the once-only intro
interaction.touch: Scroll normally on mobile — all triggers fire on touch scroll too

drops.title: Column Pager
drops.description: CSS multi-column flow turned into a book-style paginator with scroll-snap, drop caps, and pull quotes — a preview of Chrome 145's column-wrap/column-height properties.
drops.concept: Long-form text poured into CSS columns naturally creates evenly-sized 'pages' when the column box has a fixed height and horizontal scroll-snap. This drop builds a full magazine reader on that trick — with a live column-width slider, a single/spread mode toggle, drop caps, and pull quotes — while explaining how Chrome 145's new column-wrap and column-height properties extend the same idea to true vertical pagination.
drops.source: CSS-Tricks — 'New CSS Multi-Column Layout Wrapping Features in Chrome'

interaction.mouse: Click the arrows or drag the sliders in the debug panel

drops.title: Ransom Note
drops.description: 2026's 'Analog Anarchy' collage-type trend, live: type anything and watch each letter get a random font, size, rotation, and paper-scrap color.
drops.concept: A rejection of uniform type systems — mismatched fonts, jittered baselines, and torn-paper color swatches per letter, styled after cut-and-paste ransom notes. Built with a seeded PRNG so 'Shuffle' gives fully reproducible re-randomizations, three paper palettes, and tunable jitter/size-variance sliders, plus an SVG-to-canvas PNG export.
drops.source: Creative Bloq — 'Breaking rules and bringing joy: top typography trends for 2026'
tech: SVG foreignObject to canvas PNG export

interaction.mouse: Type in the input, click Shuffle for a new random layout
interaction.click: Click a palette swatch or Export PNG
interaction.touch: Full touch support for typing and buttons

drops.title: Committed
drops.description: Three widgets engineered to survive interruption: a save button that never jumps, a height-stable skeleton loader, and a spring toggle that never resets to zero.
drops.concept: Most micro-interaction demos show the happy path; this one deliberately stress-tests the unhappy ones — rapid re-clicks, simulated failures, and slow networks — following the philosophy that trust is built in the half-second after a click. A token-based cancellation guard keeps the save button's async response from clobbering a newer click, skeleton rows reserve their final height before content exists, and a hand-rolled spring toggle interpolates from its current position instead of restarting.
drops.source: ddoemonn/interior — 'micro-interactions for react, built for the half-second after a click'

interaction.click: Use the debug panel to slow the network or force a failure
interaction.touch: All three widgets are fully touch-operable

drops.title: Palette Composer
drops.description: Pick one base color and derive a full harmonious palette live — complementary, triadic, analogous, or monochrome — mirroring what CSS relative color syntax now does natively.
drops.concept: CSS relative color syntax lets you define new colors as a function of an existing one — lighten, desaturate, or rotate hue with the 'from' keyword — which is exactly what design-tool palette generators do by hand. This component reimplements that math in JS for guaranteed cross-browser results, displays the equivalent oklch(from ...) CSS for each swatch, auto-picks readable foreground text per swatch by relative luminance, and copies hex values to the clipboard on click.
drops.source: web.dev — 'Color themes with Baseline CSS features'

interaction.mouse: Pick a base color, choose a harmony mode, click a swatch to copy
interaction.click: Click any swatch to copy its hex to the clipboard
interaction.touch: Native color picker and buttons work on touch
